last_assessment.reasoning: The glossary moves substantially toward a complete lexicon by adding structural, action, entity, attribute, relation, search, platform, location, and descriptive categories. It remains incomplete and insufficiently categorized: several retained lexical forms are unresolved, attribute value categories are conflated, and required descriptive domains are not independently look-upable.

Several formerly residual attribute values now have named categories or defined rules, and the vocabulary-symbol typing inconsistency is addressed. However, content, policy, amenity, ticket, seat, code fields, medical fields, food/meal fields, and message/collaboration fields remain arbitrary STRING values; merely naming future categories does not make those values glossary symbols or glossary-derived values. The unqualified itinerary count additionally loses a required attribute constraint.

changes.grammar:
type ::= "NUMBER" | "STRING" | "BOOL" | "LIST" "[" type "]" | "REF" "[" type "]"
value ::= STRING | NUMBER | IDENT | "TRUE" | "FALSE" | list_lit | diff
list_lit ::= "[" value ("," value)* "]"
diff ::= IDENT "-" NUMBER
IDENT ::= [a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*
STRING ::= "\"" ( [^"\\\n] | "\\\"" | "\\\\" | "\\n" | "\\t" | "\\u" HEXHEXHEXHEX )* "\""
NUMBER ::= "-"? [0-9]+ ( "." [0-9]+ )? ( ("e"|"E") ("+"|"-")? [0-9]+ )?
COMMENT ::= "#" through end of physical line.
changes.semantics: As before, with one addition: a bare IDENT token that names a member of a defined vocabulary category (e.g. `role_manager`, `tone_urgent`, `art_itinerary`) is a **vocabulary symbol**. Lexically it is an IDENT (unquoted, no STRING escaping), but for all static typing purposes — RETURN type matching, LET's exact-type rule, Check comparisons, and LIST[T] element typing — a vocabulary symbol has static type STRING. This resolves the prior inconsistency where `LIST[STRING]` was declared to hold bare category symbols (e.g. itinerary stops as entity-name/location-name members) despite IDENT and STRING being distinct value forms: the rule makes that legal and precise rather than contradictory. A vocabulary symbol is never a STRING *literal* (it carries no quotes and cannot use string escapes) but it type-checks as STRING wherever STRING is required. Everything else in Types & Lexicon (REF[T], the four base types, `diff`) is unchanged.

changes.semantics: Legal Generate attributes: target, audience, content, duration, duration_unit, format, locale, quantity, style, tone, stop_min_per_day, max_walk_duration, max_walk_duration_unit. `target`'s value is an artifact-value symbol (GENERATE always produces an artifact, never an entity; Action.target stays entity-name/artifact-value split by construct, not by attribute name). `audience` -> recipient-value. `tone` -> tone-value. `format` -> format-value. `duration_unit`/`max_walk_duration_unit` -> duration-unit-value. `style` -> style-value. `locale` -> locale-value. `duration`, `quantity`, `stop_min_per_day`, `max_walk_duration` are NUMBER. `stop_min_per_day` expresses a minimum-count-per-day constraint (e.g. at least one temple per day); `max_walk_duration`+`max_walk_duration_unit` express a maximum-walking-time-between-stops constraint. changes.semantics: Unchanged validation rule (attribute must be a governed attribute-name member, category-valid, and signature-listed) plus these wirings: `color`/`size`/`gender` (product-attribute-value) and `shape` (shape-value, new) are now legal on `search_web` and `pick_up` so product search/selection can carry physical descriptors (e.g. a gray round mirror). `state` (state-value, new) is legal on `pick_up` and `place` so an object's required or resulting condition (warm, clean, microwaved) can be asserted when selecting/placing it, without requiring an extra heat/rinse step when the object is merely being identified by state. `browse_trending` is a new operation for browsing a platform's currently-popular items/searches by location; its `target` is an entity-name symbol for the thing browsed (e.g. `trending_searches`, pending addition — quoted-string transitional exception applies per entity-name's rule until added). `discount_percent` (NUMBER, 0-100) is now legal on `offer_discount` to express a percentage discount. `check_support_status`'s `metric` attribute now also accepts order/customer-status members from the expanded metric-value category (e.g. order lateness, first-time vs. repeat buyer), so conditional support logic can branch on them via Check/Flow-If. Canonical ordering and handle rules are unchanged.

changes.rationale: Restores every previously-listed attribute, wires in all new categories (shape-value, state-value, style-value, locale-value, metric-value), adds the new itinerary-constraint and discount attributes, resolves the itinerary/route list-typing conflict via the Types & Lexicon fix, and gives every remaining transitional STRING attribute an explicit, named future category instead of an unstated gap.

coverage.reasoning: The added shape, state, metric, locale, style, itinerary, browsing, and discount facilities cover several previously unsupported held-out constraints, including round mirrors, full/empty rolls, support discounts, and itinerary timing. However, the proposed stop_min_per_day attribute records only a number and cannot state that the required daily stop is a temple, while several code and content attributes remain opaque STRING payloads.

expressivity.reasoning: The proposal adds first-class fields for several constraints previously hidden in content, but its itinerary example still loses the required temple category: stop_min_per_day=1 means only a count. Transitional STRING attributes continue to carry code paths, expected outcomes, policies, message structure, and substantive generation requests as prose rather than defined value sets.

determinism.reasoning: Dedicated value categories and the closed-for-encoding format rule improve convergence. Yet independent translations still diverge materially on TASK versus CONVO, target selection, status-query sequencing, artifact type, return type, and handle names; the new open categories also lack exhaustive synonym/canonicalization rules. The worked examples themselves violate the stated canonical attribute ordering.

interpretability.reasoning: Splitting state/style/locale/metric out of descriptive-value makes values easier to look up. But attribute-name calls itself a complete index while retaining dozens of unresolved future categories, and the duplicate add of the already-existing descriptive-value entry is structurally unclear. The overloaded rule that every vocabulary symbol statically counts as STRING also obscures category identity in general typed contexts.

improvement.reasoning: A weaker planner gains useful actionable structure from color, shape, state, discount percentage, support metrics, and numeric itinerary constraints. It still cannot reliably act on semantic constraints hidden in STRING content, such as the private-members feature behavior, the exact temple requirement, or a user-provided script that must be revised.

cross_check.notes: Providers exactly agree only on Limited Time Offers. For support they differ on entity targets, check sequencing, and branch structure; for toilet-paper movement they differ on source order and handle naming; for the Sphinx item one reports a gap while the other uses opaque strings; and for veganism and tweets they differ on TASK versus CONVO, artifact type, styles, and result type. The proposal improves some canonical value symbols but does not resolve these construct-selection and decomposition divergences.

required_changes.change: Change the operation from add to revise. It already exists in the current glossary, so a second entry would be duplicate and conflicting; replace its state-inclusive semantics and example with the narrowed mod_/dom_ definition.

Correct the worked example to obey its own canonical ordering: target, content, duration, duration_unit, max_walk_duration, max_walk_duration_unit, stop_min_per_day. Also add a typed symbolic requirement field, such as stop_requirement -> entity-name/category-value, so 'at least one temple per day' is not reduced to an unqualified count.

Correct the search_web worked example to its stated required-first then alphabetical optional order: target, availability, color, currency, location, max_price, shape. Do not retain examples that violate the canonical encoding rule.

Do not describe future category names as if they govern values now. For each transitional STRING attribute, explicitly state that it remains an N3 violation in the build phase and give a concrete next-step category specification; prioritize code-path-value, code-symbol-value, code-call-value, code-outcome-value, food-value, meal-value, message-structure-value, and procedure-value.

Define the semantics and value category for what a per-day minimum applies to, plus the scope of max walking duration (e.g. consecutive itinerary stops), rather than only accepting two numbers and units.
Add explicit canonical members and synonym mappings for state_full and state_empty, since they are required by the sampled household task and are not merely illustrative variants of warm/clean.

Add canonical translation rules for closed-task decomposition and for choosing TASK versus CONVO versus GENERATE. In particular, specify when status checks are hoisted, which entity is target for order/customer support actions, and the canonical artifact/result type for multi-item generation.

logic_issues: The proposal adds descriptive-value even though descriptive-value already exists. This conflicts with the stated change operation and would create duplicate normative glossary entries rather than revise the residual bucket.
Generate's Kyoto worked example violates its own canonical ordering: stop_min_per_day appears before max_walk_duration and max_walk_duration_unit, although optional attributes must be alphabetized.
Action's mirror worked example violates its own canonical ordering: availability, currency, location, max_price, and shape are not emitted in alphabetical optional-attribute order.

stop_min_per_day=1 cannot encode the source meaning 'at least one temple per day'; it expresses only an unqualified minimum count. The proposed claim that the constraint is symbolically covered is therefore overstated.

The new attribute-name entry calls itself a complete index while numerous attributes still resolve only to STRING and a named future category. Naming an eventual category is not a present value-set rule under N3.

N2.reasoning: Dedicated shape, state, style, locale, metric, and more explicit format vocabulary materially expand the descriptive lexicon, but many needed descriptive categories remain absent and their values still reside in STRING payloads.

N3.reasoning: Several formerly residual attribute values now have named categories or defined rules, and the vocabulary-symbol typing inconsistency is addressed. However, content, policy, amenity, ticket, seat, code fields, medical fields, food/meal fields, and message/collaboration fields remain arbitrary STRING values; merely naming future categories does not make those values glossary symbols or glossary-derived values. The unqualified itinerary count additionally loses a required attribute constraint.

N7.reasoning: The category splits and closed format encoding reduce value-level ambiguity, but the supplied examples violate canonical ordering and independent translations remain strongly divergent on decomposition, construct selection, targets, and handles.

N1.reasoning: Free STRING values and unrestricted identifiers remain legal in expressions. This build-phase proposal does not close them, and it does not make the existing violation worse.

N4.reasoning: All open-item simulations and several closed-item simulations still require sentence-like STRING payloads. The proposal expressly retains content as a transitional STRING channel, as permitted by the stated build-phase sequencing.

N5.reasoning: Arbitrary strings and open identifier-derived symbols remain available, so the language is not self-contained. The added categories do not worsen that pre-existing condition.

N6.reasoning: The proposal generally uses category-level syntax and permits assuming missing members in an existing category, but several real needs have only future category names rather than an existing category capable of holding them.

N8.reasoning: Fine-grained state, shape, style, locale, metric, and itinerary numeric constraints preserve distinctions rather than collapsing them. Richness remains incomplete where substantive constraints are kept in STRING and where temple-per-day cannot be represented.

critique.reasoning: [Forced acceptance after 3 attempt(s) without a clean accept — the required changes below are known issues carried forward for a future sprint to address, not resolved.] This is real progress on N3: several actionable attributes now have dedicated value categories, and the previous symbol/list typing contradiction is repaired. The bundle cannot be accepted intact because it duplicates an existing glossary construct, has canonical-order violations in normative examples, and overclaims symbolic coverage for an itinerary constraint whose required temple qualifier is absent. The listed vocabulary and type changes are self-contained, non-regressive increments and should land now.
